title: Delivery Delayed Past ETA - Wants Refund

customer_profile.name: Ethan Brooks
customer_profile.opening_message: My package was supposed to arrive two days ago. Tracking hasn’t updated and I’m tired of excuses. I want a refund or a replacement — today.
customer_profile.secret_condition: Will accept waiting if agent provides a real tracking-based update and commits to a next update time
customer_profile.personality_notes: Impatient but reasonable; wants facts and a plan.

checkpoints.description: Apologize and acknowledge frustration about the delay
checkpoints.hint_if_missed: Consider: Apologize and acknowledge their frustration before discussing policy.

checkpoints.description: Verify order identifier and check last tracking scan event
checkpoints.hint_if_missed: Consider: Ask for order identifier and reference the last tracking scan event.

checkpoints.description: Explain what the tracking status means in plain language
checkpoints.hint_if_missed: Consider: Explain the tracking status simply so the customer understands.

checkpoints.description: Provide an updated ETA or investigation timeline
checkpoints.hint_if_missed: Consider: Provide an updated ETA or a clear investigation timeline.

checkpoints.description: Offer next steps aligned with policy (investigation, replacement if 48h no movement, refund if SLA exceeded)
checkpoints.hint_if_missed: Consider: Offer policy-aligned options: replacement after 48h no movement; refund after SLA threshold.

checkpoints.description: Commit to a concrete next update time
checkpoints.hint_if_missed: Consider: Commit to the next update time to build trust.

common_mistakes_to_watch: Saying 'it will arrive soon' without checking tracking
Blaming the courier instead of taking ownership
Not giving a timeline for next update

scenario_context: Order is 2 days past ETA but not yet past refund SLA threshold (refund eligible only after 3 business days past SLA). Replacement allowed only if no tracking movement for 48 hours. Customer is frustrated but not abusive.
